meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-09 | Start: 16:00 PST | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Saha (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Thompson (Clearline SRE), Benito Ruiz (Clearline ML), Derek Chow (PM), Maya Patel (Security)
summary: POC scoping focused on parametrizing Clearline's rate profiles into Redwood's harness, handoff plan for client adapter, streaming vs non-streaming decision logic, and acceptance criteria for tail latency and error budget. Action items: share templates, sample adapter, and 48h traffic; schedule 1st harness run next week.
transcript: 00:00:04 Jordan Kim (Redwood): All right thanks everyone for joining, can you see my screen? (brief pause) I think we good, cool.

00:00:18 Derek Chow (Clearline): Yep seen. We wanted to focus today's session on how we feed our rate shapes into your harness and where the adapter sits, and also finalize acceptance criteria for latencies.

00:00:30 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Awesome. Quick agenda: we take your traffic profile, map it to the harness rate buckets, show a sample adapter for tokenized client calls, then discuss streaming fallthroughs and fallback — and wrap with next steps.
00:00:49 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): Good. FYI we have some regulatory notes — Maya's on for that. We will need audit logs and KMS integration for the PII flows.
00:01:02 Maya Patel (Clearline): yes, SOC2 is baseline, we also need encryption-at-rest with our CMK. Is that supported in the private deployment?

00:01:15 Luis Ortega (Redwood): For Private yes, we can do KMS/HSM integration; for Dedicated we have encryption and audit logs. We'll attach the security packet after the call; it's the same one we used for other healthcare customers (may be mis-typed in auto-transcript as securepack).

00:01:32 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Great. On to traffic: our peak RPS is about 450 requests per second but it's very spiky — sometimes 3x within 30s windows when promos run. We also have many long context completions, 2k token averages on some flows.

00:01:49 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Okay spikes and long context are both important. For the harness we normally accept a CSV with timestamped RPS and heatmap of sequence lengths — that lets us synthesize the rate profile. We'll share a template. The CSV should have columns: start_ts, rps, avg_seq_len — (note: schema in doc).
00:02:12 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): Quick Q: should we pre-compute KV cache hit ratios or do you want raw traces?

00:02:18 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Raw traces preferred, we can compute cache warming heuristics. If you only have aggregated histograms that's ok but raw is best. Also — if you can't share PII we can do an on-prem sniff that redacts. We'll put options in the partner doc.

00:02:40 Derek Chow (Clearline): On the adapter: our stack uses an internal gateway that rate-limits to 10k tokens/min per user, and we use a short-lived client cert scheme. How invasive is the adapter?

00:02:52 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Our adapter can run as a sidecar or as a small shim within your gateway. It just translates your request shape into the harness calls and handles streaming frames if you choose streaming. Example repo will show both sidecar and direct-call patterns.
00:03:12 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): We prefer minimal changes. Sidecar looks better. We also want to test with our rate limiter in place so the harness sees the real throttled traffic pattern.

00:03:26 Luis Ortega (Redwood): That's doable. We can replay traffic through your rate-limiter in a staging route and capture the effective RPS the harness will see. That also surfaces 429s and retry behavior — important for acceptance.
00:03:41 Maya Patel (Clearline): On compliance, does the harness persist any payloads? We need log redaction and retention controls.

00:03:48 Jordan Kim (Redwood): By default we don't persist content beyond the trace window unless you opt into full recording; logs can be redacted and retention is configurable. We'll send the retention SLA doc.

00:04:02 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Back to streaming vs non-streaming: two failure modes to consider. With streaming, your client sees partial tokens quickly, which is lower perceived latency, but more open TCP connections and a different error surface when a backend fallback occurs. Non-streaming gives you a single aggregated response and simplifies the harness but will increase tail latency measured at the client.
00:04:28 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): For clinical text generation we prefer eventual full response over partial outputs, but in chat flows we like streaming. Can we mix both in the same POC?

00:04:36 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Yes. We recommend splitting workloads: 70% non-streaming batch for long completions and 30% streaming for low-latency chat. The harness can run both profiles in parallel and report combined SLO adherence.
00:04:55 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): How do we parameterize that? Our config is per-route currently.

00:05:02 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): The rate-profile CSV can include a route column. Example: route_name, start_ts, rps, stream_flag, avg_seq_len. The harness will fork requests to the streaming path for rows with stream_flag=1.
00:05:17 Derek Chow (Clearline): Nice. What about retries? Our gateway will retry on 5xx with exponential backoff which can create retry storms; is there protection in the harness to model that?

00:05:27 Luis Ortega (Redwood): We can model client-side backoff behavior in the adapter. We'll also simulate cascading retries in the harness to test circuit breaker settings. We usually run a sensitivity sweep for retry_multiplier and max_inflight to find stable SLO regions.
00:05:46 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Can the harness simulate KV cache warmup? Some of our flows are cache-sensitive and cold starts spike p99 by 600ms.

00:05:53 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Yes, we have a warmup mode. You can provide warmup traces (a short sequence of representative calls) or let the harness replay a warmup window prior to the main run. We'll also expose a kv_cache_warmup parameter in the run config.
00:06:11 Maya Patel (Clearline): For SLOs we want p50/p95/p99 and a hard p99.9 ceiling for patient-facing flows. Also error budget of 0.1% per day. Is that realistic?

00:06:24 Jordan Kim (Redwood): It's tight but possible with Dedicated or Private, depends on batch sizes and autoscale thresholds. For hosted, p99.9 at 2k contexts is challenging without reserved capacity.
00:06:36 Derek Chow (Clearline): We'd like to measure cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for our workload — can you produce a per-token cost projection from the harness runs?

00:06:45 Luis Ortega (Redwood): Yes. After the run we provide a token-level cost breakdown and per-route cost rates, including batch efficiency gains and quantization suggestions where applicable. We'll annotate the run results with recommended model variants.

00:07:02 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Speaking of models: we use an open LLM for gen currently; any model constraints for streaming? We've seen models that don't stream cleanly and produce truncation artifacts.

00:07:12 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): We'll test model variants. Note that some models require a special streaming codec or different kernel paths; we'll recommend a streaming-compatible variant in the model catalog. The harness records any truncation artifacts as a quality regression signal.
00:07:29 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): What's the expected timeline for the POC?

00:07:33 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Typical: 1 week to exchange artifacts and prep, 1 week for harness run and iterations, 1 week for validation and security sign-off — so about three weeks end-to-end. We can compress to two if you provide the trace and prompts today.
00:07:49 Maya Patel (Clearline): Security review will take at least a week from our side. Let's assume 3 weeks then.

00:07:55 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): For the run config we'll need: traffic CSV, 48h trace (if possible), warmup traces, route mapping, and three golden prompts. Also define acceptance gates: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 750ms for non-streaming patient flows, p99.9 < 1200ms optional for dedicated. For streaming chat, median token latency under 30ms and end-to-end p95 < 400ms.
00:08:22 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Those are good starting points. The non-streaming numbers are aggressive for long contexts — can we add a sliding acceptance window by sequence length?
00:08:30 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Absolutely — we can partition SLOs by seq_len buckets, e.g., <512 tokens, 512-1500, >1500. Each bucket has its own p95/p99 targets and weight in the combined SLA.
00:08:44 Derek Chow (Clearline): How do we visualize results? We need per-route dashboards and traces to show to infra and product.

00:08:50 Luis Ortega (Redwood): We provide per-run dashboards in the Console export and a CSV of per-request telemetry. The Console will include token cost, latency histograms, failure traces, and sample outputs flagged for hallucination or truncation.
00:09:04 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): About telemetry fields — we need correlation IDs and user_id redaction. Can the adapter inject our trace IDs into the harness logs?
00:09:12 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Yes, adapter supports passing through X-Trace-Id and other headers; we persist correlation ids for the run and they can be redacted in stored logs.
00:09:26 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Are there limits on concurrent connections for streaming? We expect ~1k concurrent streaming connections during peaks.
00:09:33 Luis Ortega (Redwood): On Dedicated, 1k concurrent streams is ok but we'll want to tune keepalive and rps_per_instance. We'll propose instance counts after the first harness run.
00:09:46 Maya Patel (Clearline): Any known gotchas integrating client cert auth?

00:09:51 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): We support mTLS and client certs. In sidecar mode the certificate exchange is handled by the sidecar and not by the harness. We'll include a deployment snippet for your gateway.
00:10:05 Derek Chow (Clearline): Let's talk failure scenarios: if the streaming connection drops mid-response, what's shown to the client?

00:10:12 Luis Ortega (Redwood): If streaming drops we surface an explicit error frame and the adapter can attempt a resume if the model supports streaming continuation. Otherwise the client gets a truncated output and a 5xx — the harness will flag these as high severity for the run.
00:10:29 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Can the harness replay partial failures to test our client resume logic?

00:10:34 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Yes, we have failure injection options: drop-n-percent, close-after-n-tokens, and artificial slowbacks. We'll include those in the run config so you can validate resume and retry behavior.
00:10:48 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): Great. For acceptance criteria, we also want to include quality checks on the golden prompts — like BLEU or ROUGE thresholds or a small eval harness.
00:10:57 Jordan Kim (Redwood): We can add a quality eval stage post-run that checks outputs against expected references and surface any regressions. That will be part of the results bundle.
00:11:06 Derek Chow (Clearline): Perfect. Any dependencies from Redwood side?

00:11:10 Jordan Kim (Redwood): We need GH access to a private repo for the adapter sample, access to the trace (S3 or secure share), and a brief infra diagram of your gateway flow. We'll add a checklist to the Slack thread.
00:11:23 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): For the trace, we will mask PII and produce a synthetic variant if required. Which do you prefer?
00:11:29 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Raw masked traces are best. Synthetic is fine but sometimes synthetic traffic misses edge cases in sequence length distributions.
00:11:38 Maya Patel (Clearline): We'll try masked raw traces then. On compliance sign-off, expect at minimum one security review meeting.
00:11:45 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Understood — we'll prepare the security packet and an initial risk register for the review.

00:11:54 Derek Chow (Clearline): Let's pin the timeline: Jordan to send artifacts by Friday the 11th, sample run the following week, results and validation the week after — three-week plan. Is that synced?
00:12:06 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Yeah that'll work. I'll put tentative calendar invites for the run window and the post-run review.

00:12:12 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Quick note on metrics: please include p50/p95/p99/p99.9 in the telemetry exports and annotate by route + seq_len bucket; the harness will output both absolute and normalized token-cost per route.
00:12:28 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): Sounds good. One more: does Redwood support token-level streaming ACKs? We have a client that wants acknowledgement per-chunk for analytics.

00:12:36 Luis Ortega (Redwood): We currently stream chunks but we can surface chunk-level metadata (token counts, partial confidence) as part of the streaming envelope — we'll show an example in the adapter repo.
00:12:49 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): Okay, let's move into a short walkthrough of the CSV template you mentioned — can you share on screen?

00:12:54 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): (shares) here's the template — route, start_ts, rps, stream_flag, avg_seq_len, kv_cache_hit_estimate. A small sample row: chat-main, 2026-11-11T09:00Z, 200, 1, 64, 0.35
00:13:20 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): That kv_cache_hit_estimate field: should it be decimal or percent? The template example is 0.35 meaning 35%?
00:13:27 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Decimal is fine. We'll accept both but will normalize on ingestion. Also optional columns: retry_profile, auth_scheme.
00:13:39 Derek Chow (Clearline): Any suggestions for bin size on seq_len buckets?
00:13:42 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): We recommend <256, 256-1024, 1024-2048, >2048. If you have a heavy tail above 2k keep an extra bucket.
00:13:52 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): We'll format the CSV and send. We also want to test a scenario with a simulated promotional spike — 3x baseline for 45s. Can the harness do short spike windows?
00:13:59 Luis Ortega (Redwood): Yes, spike windows and randomized jitter are supported. We'll include stress profile configs in the run template.
00:14:10 Maya Patel (Clearline): Regarding logs retention, we need logs held for 90 days and then automatic purge. Is that doable for the POC?

00:14:16 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Yes, retention config is flexible. For POC we normally keep 14 days by default but we can set 90 days for your run if requested — there may be storage surcharge, we'll note that in the pricing follow-up.
00:14:29 Derek Chow (Clearline): Pricing follow-up would be great — we need a cost delta between 90d and 14d retention and Dedicated vs Hosted options.
00:14:36 Jordan Kim (Redwood): We'll include that in the follow-up email and spreadsheet. Also we'll annotate which costs are amortized vs per-run.
00:14:46 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): For the adapter sample — can you support Node and Go runtimes? Our gateway team uses Go.
00:14:52 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): We'll provide both Node and Go examples. The Go adapter will include TLS config and a small integration test.
00:15:02 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): Great. Any other risk items?
00:15:06 Maya Patel (Clearline): I want to ensure we have a rollback plan if the harness uncovered a regression in the model that impacts clinical outputs.

00:15:13 Jordan Kim (Redwood): We'll block a canary and fallback policy in the config: if quality regressions exceed threshold we route to a safe-model fallback and halt rollout. That's part of Redwood Optimize suggestions.
00:15:24 Derek Chow (Clearline): Can you record a short demo of the adapter deploy we can hand to infra?
00:15:28 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): Yes, Priya will record a 6-8 minute screencap showing sidecar deploy and sample curl flows.
00:15:35 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): ok great. Are we missing anything?
00:15:38 Jordan Kim (Redwood): I don't think so — let's recap next steps (brief silence).

00:15:46 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Recap: I'll send rate-profile template and retention/pricing notes by Fri 12/11; Priya will push adapter examples and a short screencap by 12/13; Aisha will provide masked 48h trace by 12/16; we target harness run w/c 12/14 and post-run review week of 12/21. Security review meeting to be scheduled separately.
00:16:12 Derek Chow (Clearline): That's clear. Thanks everyone. We'll expect the GH link and the template.
00:16:18 Maya Patel (Clearline): Thanks — see you on the security call.
00:16:21 Jordan Kim (Redwood): Thanks all. Ending recording.
00:16:25 (meeting ends, remainder of time used for side-channel questions — transcription picks up brief chatter)
00:17:12 Benito Ruiz (Clearline): (off-record) do you have a sample mapping of our rate-limiter to the harness?
00:17:18 Priya Saha (Redwood SE): I'll DM a mapping spreadsheet after the call.
00:18:02 Aisha Thompson (Clearline): (off-record) also need contact for security reviewer
00:18:06 Jordan Kim (Redwood): I'll copy Maya and share the security reviewer contact.
